pictures.name: header
pictures.alt: Illustration of a glowing glass cane with a hot, newly rounded swirl marble at its end, held between the blades of a pair of marble scissors.
pictures.caption: A marble cut from a glass cane with marble scissors. Illustration.

pictures.name: cane-cut
pictures.alt: Illustration of the five steps of making a cane-cut marble: make a glass cane with the design inside, heat its end until soft, round it off, twist it for the spiral, and cut it free with the marble scissors.
pictures.caption: Cane-cut marbles in five steps. Illustration.

pictures.name: single-gather
pictures.alt: Illustration of a single-gather marble: a ball of hot glass built up in layers on the end of a metal rod called a punty.
pictures.caption: A single-gather marble is built up on a punty, then rounded and cut free. Illustration.

pictures.name: pontil
pictures.alt: Illustration of a handmade swirl marble with its pontil mark, the small rough spot at one pole where it was cut free, circled.
pictures.caption: Every handmade marble has a pontil: a small rough spot where it was cut free. Illustration.

pictures.name: christensen-machine
pictures.alt: Diagram of the principle of Christensen's marble machine: two grooved rolls turning in opposite directions roll a lump of soft glass into a ball between them, with a spring letting one roll move aside when the ball is big enough.
pictures.caption: Christensen's machine (patent filed 1902, published 1905): two grooved rolls turning in opposite directions. A simplified illustration, not a copy of the patent drawing.

pictures.name: machine-method
pictures.alt: Illustration of the machine method in five numbered steps: glass melted in a furnace, a stream of molten glass, a rotating shear cutting a gob, spiral-grooved rollers turning it into a sphere, and finished marbles collected to cool.
pictures.caption: The machine method: melt, stream, cut, roll, collect. Illustration.

pictures.name: colour
pictures.alt: Illustration of where a marble's colour comes from: a handmade marble's coloured rods built into the cane, a machine-made marble's streams of coloured glass flowing together, and a cat's eye's coloured vanes injected into clear glass.
pictures.caption: Where the colour comes from: the cane, the glass streams, or vanes injected into clear glass. Illustration.

pictures.name: annealing
pictures.alt: Illustration of annealing: marbles travelling on a conveyor through a long oven called a lehr, from hot at one end to cool at the other.
pictures.caption: Annealing: the glass cools slowly in a lehr so it doesn't crack later. Illustration.

pictures.name: share
pictures.alt: How glass marbles are made. Illustrated glass marbles: a handmade swirl, a Lutz, an onionskin and a clearie.
